scope: Controlled synthetic recommendation mechanism probe; not BEAM or a representative memory benchmark.

models.qualificationCaveat: Gateway alias is not a verified model snapshot.

policy.scope: Controlled synthetic recommendation mechanism probe; not BEAM or a representative memory benchmark.
policy.program: One host-supplied typed recommendation query and identical candidate universe, source eligibility, positive rule joins, conflict handling, and deterministic rendering for exact and Jev arms. No model-generated query compiler in this first probe.
policy.semanticTask: Directed source support for a proposed item field; exact values and references only. Model judgments remain unverified semantic premises.
policy.semanticAdmission: Admit only selected supported choices. Confidence and probabilities are reported as diagnostics, without tuning a threshold or interpreting them as proof truth.
policy.readerPromptProvenance: The registered profile supplies transport/model settings and a 600-second deadline. Its readerContract is catalog metadata, not the executed prompt. The exact V5 writer prompt and request bodies are frozen in the plan.
policy.readerAccounting: Byte-bounded native request; same existing Gateway campaign/store and selected project authority. No paid judge: deterministic fixed-schema scoring.
policy.comparison: Whole-case and field correctness, supported-field coverage, emitted-field precision, abstention, conflict, malformed output, latency and cost. Jev-program versus exact-program isolates semantic admission. Either program versus writer changes the answer-program bundle.
policy.baseline: All-unknown usefulness control accompanies results and cannot qualify as a useful answer merely by withholding fields.
policy.promotion: No automatic production or BEAM-confirmation promotion from this synthetic probe. Freeze all source, gold, program and request bytes before provider calls; report every planned case.

fixturePolicy.sourceAuthority: Synthetic host-authored records only. Authority and strictly increasing supersession order are supplied metadata, not model judgments.
fixturePolicy.candidateConstruction: Manually annotated whole-field spans paired with every requested item in source order, then item order. All arms may admit only supplied eligible candidates; no other field extraction, even when source prose could support it. No gold filtering.
fixturePolicy.eligibility: Exclude any record explicitly superseded by a later host record. For title candidates require exact equality with the locked requested display title. Both arms apply the identical policy.
fixturePolicy.exactGrammar: Audiobook <JSON string of displayTitle>: <title|narrator> = <JSON string of field value>. Entire source statement must equal this byte-for-byte.
fixturePolicy.semanticTask: Does the whole source statement establish that this named audiobook has this field value? Directed source attribution only; supported, contradicted, uncertain. No world knowledge, inferred missing metadata, or name substitution.
fixturePolicy.admission: Only supported admits a semantic candidate. Contradicted and uncertain preserve missingness. Neither model confidence nor edge scores are proof probabilities.
fixturePolicy.outcome: Same pure recommendation program and renderer after admission: complete title+narrator recommends; incomplete optional omits; incomplete requested is unknown; distinct admitted values conflict.
fixturePolicy.limits: No source clipping or candidate truncation. Every input/field/call overflow fails the protocol.
fixturePolicy.design: 8 direct controls, 6 paraphrase controls, 6 adversarial controls. Controlled mechanism evidence only, not representative memory or BEAM quality.
fixturePolicy.goldIsolation: V5_GOLD is not nested in buildFixtures output and must not be read during candidate/request construction.
fixturePolicy.goldComparison: For recommended items compare status, exact title and exact narrator. For unknown/omitted-incomplete compare status only; retained partial fields do not affect outcome equality. Binding admissions are scored separately. No fixture expects a conflict.

jev.interpretation: Captured per-request service times; the sum is not end-to-end wall latency or an Algal overhead measurement.

writer.interpretation: Captured per-request service times; the sum is not end-to-end wall latency or an Algal overhead measurement.

interpretation: Authored development cases with manually supplied spans and locked item identities. Whole-case outcomes compare all arms. Field precision and coverage count only recommended fields shared by the writer schema and programs; coverage denominator is all distinct gold-supported item/field slots, including slots in incomplete items. Retained partial program bindings are assessed separately by candidate scores. No confidence intervals or generalization claims from this fixture set.

demonstrated: Ordinary two-cell Algal manifest invokes the pure Oh recommendation program through a host FnRegistry.
Direct and Algal-hosted JSON outputs match, including a requested unknown item.
Serialized run receipt replays offline with the same digest.
Mirrored output forgery is rejected by Algal replay.
Host rejects source/manifest/input pin drift, executable accessors and oversized input.

negativeSemanticControl.result: An intentionally wrong admitted semantic premise that swaps title and narrator still replays successfully.
negativeSemanticControl.meaning: Replay proves deterministic execution consistency conditional on admitted bindings; it does not validate semantic entailment, entity identity, authority, freshness or real-world truth.

limits.scope: Private TypeScript compatibility host; no Algal or public Oh runtime changes.
limits.performance: Algal function cost is modeled host work, not the actual Oh projection work count, CPU time, latency or financial cost.
limits.trust: The host registry and pinned Oh implementation remain trusted executable code. No Rust/native parity, process isolation, deployment, production integration or general memory-correctness claim.

conclusions: This authored candidate-admission probe is not a representative retrieval or memory benchmark.
C minus B measures semantic admission against the deliberately strict exact grammar, with the same deterministic program.
C minus A compares a semantic binding/program bundle with the ordinary source-reading writer under the restricted inventory.
Replay and source-span integrity do not establish semantic entailment or real-world truth.
No production default, Algal language change or automatic benchmark promotion follows from this probe.
